headline: Validating predicted omics layers inferred from histology and spatial transcriptomics
label: Spatial Omics Model Evaluation
summary: Recent preprints frame cross-modal omics prediction as a validation problem, testing whether inferred molecular layers match measured ground truth.
synthesis: The dominant thread is treating the predicted omics layer itself as the object under validation. A benchmark of cross-slice protein imputation compares learning-based and alignment-based methods, and TSNR predicts spatial protein abundance from spatial transcriptomics using protein-specific center signals and a robust training objective. PatHoST reconstructs pathogen spatial distributions from host spatial transcriptomics, validated with M. abscessus benchmarking. The histology-driven work, a multi-scale graph neural network predicting bulk, spatial, and single-cell transcriptomics from whole-slide images and HistoTx's early fusion of H&E patches with transcript tokens, is presented mainly through architecture and training design rather than recovery tests. CMVAE, GOTSurv, and DMG-PoE address survival prognosis from single-omic, cross-sectional, and multi-omics data, so the set is heterogeneous. What is new is the emphasis on whether inferred layers are genuinely recovered.
